mainTopic: The sources of a תנא on מעשר בהמה, רבי ישמעאל בן סתריאל's testimonies, and the משנה of the three גרנות and the tithing new year
overview: The amud opens by finishing the identification of a תנא who brings יוצא דופן, מחוסר זמן, and יתום into the pen for מעשר בהמה. He follows רבי שמעון on a caesarean birth, רבי שמעון בן יהודה on מחוסר זמן, and רבי יהושע on a 'יתום' whose mother's hide (שלח) still exists. רבי ישמעאל בן סתריאל then testifies before רבי that in his town they dress a newborn in its dead mother's skin, and רבי says this reveals the reason of the משנה. He adds wonder-reports about huge lettuce, a giant cedar, and a בר יוכני egg that flooded sixty cities. The גמרא questions the egg story from a פסוק, and רב אשי answers that it was an unfertilized egg. A new משנה then lists the three yearly deadlines (גרנות) for מעשר בהמה and records the opinions of רבי עקיבא, בן עזאי, and רבי אלעזר with רבי שמעון. It also gives the dispute over whether the tithing year begins on 1 אלול or 1 תשרי. The משנה explains that ראש השנה divides the groups of animals, while a גורן only marks when slaughtering untithed animals becomes forbidden. The גמרא asks why there are three גרנות, and רבה בר שילא answers that there is one for each birthing season. It then asks why these particular times were chosen, and רבי תנחום's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The תנא holds like רבי שמעון on a caesarean-born animal
steps.stepSummary: The תנא who counts יוצא דופן for tithing follows רבי שמעון, who says such a birth is a full, proper birth. This goes against רבי יוחנן's understanding of רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי שמעון, who said: a יוצא דופן is a full-fledged offspring. And this is not like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining whose opinion this תנא follows. He includes a יוצא דופן in מעשר בהמה because he holds like רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says a child born by caesarean is a real 'ולד', a real birth. So a caesarean-born animal is fit and must be tithed. רבי יוחנן understood that רבי שמעון agrees such an animal is unfit for קדשים. If so, this תנא could not be following רבי שמעון. So the גמרא says openly that this תנא does not follow רבי יוחנן's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: An offspring born through the side wall (caesarean birth)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not like רבי יוחנן' does not mean רבי יוחנן argues with רבי שמעון. It means this תנא does not follow רבי יוחנן's claim about what רבי שמעון holds for קדשים.

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
who said: one born by caesarean section —
is a full-fledged offspring,
and not in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן (נדה מ.) holds that רבי שמעון concedes a caesarean-born animal is unfit for קדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier identification of the תנא's sources (on the previous amud).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On יוצא דופן, the תנא follows רבי שמעון, who says it is a full birth, and does not follow רבי יוחנן's reading of him.

steps.title: מחוסר זמן follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה, and יתום means the hide still exists
steps.stepSummary: On מחוסר זמן, the תנא follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה. His יתום case is one where the mother's hide is still present, so the animal is not truly an orphan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding an animal whose time has not yet come, he holds like רבי שמעון בן יהודה. As for the orphan: this is where the hide still exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next two items on the תנא's list. It names his source for מחוסר זמן and explains what he means by יתום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יהודה holds that a מחוסר זמן still enters the pen to be tithed. A true יתום is exempt from tithing. So the גמרא says this 'יתום' is really a case where the mother's hide (שלח) is present. In that case the animal is not counted as an orphan at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal under eight days old, not yet fit to be offered
An orphan animal whose mother died at its birth (exempt from tithe)
For example; in a case where

phrases.english: With regard to one whose time has not yet arrived

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda,
an orphan — this is where the hide exists,

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְחוּסַּר זְמַן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the same list of items, after יוצא דופן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מחוסר זמן follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה. The 'יתום' is a case where the mother's hide exists, so it is not a real orphan.

steps.title: רבי יהושע consistently holds that the hide prevents orphan status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows this fits רבי יהושע's known view. Even if the mother was slaughtered, as long as her hide exists, the newborn is not a יתום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע follows his own reasoning, for he said: even if he slaughtered its mother, if the hide exists, this is not an orphan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the 'hide exists' explanation. It points to רבי יהושע's statement in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'hide exists' case is not invented. רבי יהושע already rules that a surviving hide cancels orphan status, even when the mother was slaughtered. So the תנא is following a known, consistent view (לטעמיה).

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own (consistent) line of reasoning

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua follows his own reasoning,
for he said: even if one slaughtered its mother
and the hide exists —
this is not an orphan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2's definition of יתום by tying it to רבי יהושע's known position.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'יתום' of this תנא is a case where the hide exists.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's statement: even if the mother was slaughtered, if the hide exists it is not a יתום.
steps.whatToRemember: This תנא includes יוצא דופן (like רבי שמעון), מחוסר זמן (like רבי שמעון בן יהודה), and a 'יתום' whose mother's hide exists (like רבי יהושע).

steps.title: Testimony: newborns are dressed in the dead mother's skin
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן סתריאל of ערקת לבנה tells רבי about a local custom. When a mother animal dies, they skin her and wrap the living newborn in her hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל בן סתריאל of ערקת לבנה testified before רבי: In our place, they flay the dead mother and clothe the living one.
steps.whatsHappening: A sage reports a real farming custom from his town. This sets up רבי's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The custom shows that the mother's hide actually functions as a substitute mother for the newborn. It warms and protects the baby animal. This is new, practical information about why the hide matters.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael ben Satriel testified
from Arkat Leveina, before Rabbi:
In our place they flay the dead mother
and clothe the living newborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן סַתְרִיאֵל מֵעַרְקַת לִבְנָה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-world background to the 'hide exists' rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In his locale, a dead mother animal's hide is put on the living newborn.

steps.title: רבי: the reason of our משנה is now revealed
steps.stepSummary: רבי says this custom explains why the משנה rules that a newborn is not a יתום when the mother's hide exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: The reason of our משנה has been revealed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי connects the testimony to the משנה. He concludes that the hide counts as a replacement for the mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the rule 'hide exists means no orphan' could seem strange. The custom shows the hide really serves the newborn like a mother would. So the newborn is not fully orphaned.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the logic behind רבי יהושע's rule: the hide acts as a substitute mother, so the animal stays subject to מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: Rabbi said: The reason has been revealed
of our mishna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִתְגַּלָּה טַעְמָהּ שֶׁל מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic lesson from the testimony in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The mother's hide serves as a substitute mother, so a newborn whose mother's hide exists is not a יתום.

steps.title: Testimony: the giant lettuce of his town
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן סתריאל adds another report: the lettuce in his town has 600,000 leaves in its core.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lettuce in our place has six hundred thousand leaves in its core.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves away from the halacha. It lists more of this sage's remarkable testimonies about his hometown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is אגדה, not a legal step. It shows the amazing fertility of his region. It is attached here because the same sage gave these reports before רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally the omasum, a stomach chamber; here, the inner core of the lettuce head

steps.confusionAlert: Despite the spelling חזירין, this is not about pigs. Sefaria and the commentators read it as חזרין, lettuce.

phrases.english: The lettuce in our place
has six hundred thousand leaves
in its core (omasum),

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזֵירִין שֶׁבִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ יֵשׁ לָהֶם שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא קְלָפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further testimony by the same sage, unrelated to the halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lettuce in his locale was enormous, with 600,000 leaves in its core.

steps.title: Testimony: a fallen cedar so wide sixteen wagons crossed it
steps.stepSummary: He also reports that a cedar in his town fell, and its trunk was so wide that sixteen wagons drove side by side across it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once a cedar in our place fell, and sixteen wagons passed over its back side by side.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the list of wonder-testimonies. It describes the huge size of a local cedar tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the lettuce, this is אגדה showing how blessed his land was. 'On its back, as one' means the wagons drove across the fallen trunk side by side at the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: Its back/surface (the width of the trunk)

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת נָפַל אֶרֶז אֶחָד שֶׁבִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ,
phrases.english: Once, one cedar in our place fell,
and sixteen wagons passed
over its back as one (side by side).

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת נָפַל אֶרֶז אֶחָד שֶׁבִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another wonder-testimony in the same series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fallen cedar in his locale was wide enough for sixteen wagons to cross it side by side.

steps.title: The giant egg that flooded sixty cities
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן סתריאל reports that an egg of the בר יוכני bird once fell, drowned sixty cities, and broke three hundred cedars.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once an egg of the בר יוכני bird fell. It drowned sixty cities and broke three hundred cedar trees.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last of רבי ישמעאל בן סתריאל's amazing reports to רבי. This time he describes an enormous bird's egg that fell and caused huge damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the lettuce and the cedar before it, this story shows how huge things were in nature. The size of the egg is the whole point: its contents flooded whole cities. This report sets up the גמרא's next question.

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת נָפְלָה בֵּיצַת בַּר יוֹכָנִי,
phrases.english: Once an egg of the bar yokhani bird fell,
and it drowned sixty cities,
and it broke three hundred cedars.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת נָפְלָה בֵּיצַת בַּר יוֹכָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third wonder report in the same series as the lettuce and the cedar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg of the בר יוכני fell and caused massive flooding and destruction.

steps.title: But this bird lays its eggs on the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the egg could 'fall' at all, since a פסוק says this bird leaves its eggs on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this bird drop its eggs? But it is written: 'The כנף רננים rejoices' (and the פסוק goes on to say it leaves its eggs on the ground).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. A פסוק in איוב describes this bird as laying its eggs on the earth, so how could an egg fall from high up?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים understood כנף רננים to be the same bird as בר יוכני. The פסוק continues: 'for she leaves her eggs on the earth.' If the eggs are laid on the ground, it is hard to explain a falling egg.

keyTerms.meaning: And does it throw it? (a challenging question)
But isn't it written (introduces a verse used as a challenge)
A bird named in איוב, identified with the בר יוכני

steps.confusionAlert: Only the opening words of the פסוק are quoted. The part that actually creates the question, 'she leaves her eggs on the earth' (איוב 39:14), is in the next verse of איוב. The גמרא does not quote it and assumes the learner knows it.

phrases.english: And does it throw it down?
But isn't it written:
"The kenaf renanim rejoices"!
phrases.notes: The verse continues: 'she leaves her eggs on the earth' (איוב 39:13–14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the egg story from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a בר יוכני egg fell.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says this bird lays its eggs on the ground, so its eggs should not fall from a height.

steps.title: It was an unfertilized egg
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that this egg was unfertilized, so the bird threw it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That egg was an unfertilized egg.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי resolves the challenge. Normally the bird lays its eggs on the ground, but this particular egg was a dud, so the bird threw it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the bird's normal practice with good eggs. An egg that would never hatch is useless to the bird, so it was thrown away, and that is how it fell. The story and the פסוק no longer conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: An unfertilized (or spoiled) egg that will not hatch

steps.whatToRemember: The wonder reports end here. The פסוק about the bird describes its normal eggs, and a dud egg is the exception that the bird throws away.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
That one was an unfertilized egg.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָהוּא מוּזַרְתָּא הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the פסוק describes normal eggs, and this one was an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird never drops its eggs, so the story seems impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unfertilized egg is thrown away, so it can fall.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי עקיבא's three tithing deadlines
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. רבי עקיבא says there are three yearly deadlines for מעשר בהמה: shortly before פסח, before עצרת, and before סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are three gathering times for animal tithe: near פסח, near שבועות, and near סוכות. These are the gathering times for animal tithe. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה begins on a new topic: when during the year a person must tithe their newborn animals. רבי עקיבא names three times, each one shortly before a festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גורן is a deadline. Once it arrives, the newborn animals must be tithed, and the owner may not eat them before that. פרס means about fifteen days (half of thirty) before the festival. That way people have animals ready to bring for the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'threshing floors'; here, the deadlines for tithing animals
The animal tithe, which is every tenth newborn animal
About fifteen days (half of thirty) before a festival

steps.confusionAlert: גרנות here does not mean actual threshing floors. It borrows the idea that grain must be tithed once it reaches the threshing floor, and uses it to mean the date when animals must be tithed.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
There are three gathering times for animal tithe:
about fifteen days before Pesach,
and about fifteen days before Shavuot,
and about fifteen days before Sukkot,
and these are the gathering times of animal tithe,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, unrelated to the reports.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the three deadlines for מעשר בהמה fall about fifteen days before פסח, שבועות, and סוכות.

steps.title: בן עזאי's dates
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי gives the deadlines as exact dates: 29 אדר, 1 סיון, and 29 אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: On the twenty-ninth of אדר, on the first of סיון, and on the twenty-ninth of אב.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה. בן עזאי lists three specific calendar dates instead of 'near the festival'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives exact calendar dates. Only 29 אדר is about fifteen days before its festival (פסח); 1 סיון is just five days before שבועות, and 29 אב is far earlier than fifteen days before סוכות. His last date falls the day before 1 אלול, which connects to his doubt about when the animal-tithe year begins, brought out later in the משנה (step 17).

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
on the twenty-ninth of Adar,
on the first of Sivan,
on the twenty-ninth of Av.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בַּאֲדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different view on the dates of the three deadlines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן עזאי, the deadlines are 29 אדר, 1 סיון, and 29 אב.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון's dates
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון give the deadlines as 1 ניסן, 1 סיון, and 29 אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: On the first of ניסן, on the first of סיון, and on the twenty-ninth of אלול.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the משנה. These two תנאים put the last deadline at the very end of the year, on 29 אלול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their last deadline is the day before ראש השנה. This implies that for them the animal-tithe year begins on 1 תשרי. Their unusual choice of 29 אלול instead of 1 תשרי sets up the משנה's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (here, רבי אלעזר בן שמוע)
The last month before ראש השנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
on the first of Nisan, on the first of Sivan,
on the twenty-ninth of Elul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view on the deadlines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the deadlines are 1 ניסן, 1 סיון, and 29 אלול.

steps.title: Why 29 אלול and not 1 תשרי?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון chose 29 אלול rather than 1 תשרי, the start of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they say the twenty-ninth of אלול, and not the first of תשרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה itself asks a question about the last opinion. It is setting up an explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their other two dates fall on the first of a month, so 1 תשרי would seem more natural. The question points out that 29 אלול breaks the pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: And why did they say (introduces an explanation)

phrases.english: And why did they say the twenty-ninth of Elul
and did not say the first of Tishrei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the last date given in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the third deadline is 29 אלול rather than 1 תשרי.

steps.title: Because one cannot tithe on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: 1 תשרי is ראש השנה, a יום טוב, and tithing is not allowed on יום טוב. So they moved the deadline one day earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a יום טוב, and it is impossible to tithe on a יום טוב. Therefore they moved it earlier, to the twenty-ninth of אלול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. The real deadline would be 1 תשרי, but that day is ראש השנה, so it was moved back to the day before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing animals involves counting them and marking every tenth one with paint, which is not done on יום טוב. So the deadline was moved earlier to 29 אלול. The year boundary itself stays at 1 תשרי.

phrases.english: Because it is a festival,
and it is impossible to tithe on a festival —
therefore they moved it earlier, to the twenty-ninth of Elul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 1 תשרי is ראש השנה, and one cannot tithe on יום טוב, so the deadline was moved earlier to 29 אלול.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the animal-tithe year starts 1 אלול
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the new year for מעשר בהמה is 1 אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: The first of אלול is the new year for מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion about when the animal-tithe year begins. רבי מאיר says it starts a month before ראש השנה, on 1 אלול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'new year' matters because animals born in one year may not be tithed together with animals born in another year. רבי מאיר puts the year boundary at 1 אלול. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון put it at 1 תשרי, which is why their last deadline was the end of אלול.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of the year for animal tithe

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the four 'new years' listed in the first משנה of ראש השנה. The disagreement here is the source of that dispute.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
on the first of Elul
is the new year for animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different year boundary from the 1 תשרי implied in steps 13–15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the animal-tithe year begins on 1 אלול.

steps.title: בן עזאי: animals born in אלול are tithed separately
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי rules that animals born in אלול are tithed as their own group, because of the doubt about when the year begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: The אלול animals are tithed by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי gives a practical solution. Since we are unsure whether the year begins in אלול or in תשרי, animals born in אלול are tithed as a separate group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר is right, the אלול animals belong to the new year. If רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון are right, they belong to the old year. Tithing them separately avoids mixing years either way. This also explains why בן עזאי's own last deadline was 29 אב, before the doubtful month.

keyTerms.meaning: Are tithed by themselves, as a separate group

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the animal-tithe year. רבי מאיר says it begins 1 אלול. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say 1 תשרי. בן עזאי is in doubt, so he tithes the אלול-born animals separately.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
the Elul-born animals are tithed by themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: הָאֱלוּלִים מִתְעַשְּׂרִים בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the dispute between רבי מאיר (step 16) and רבי אלעזר with רבי שמעון (step 13).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals born in אלול form their own group for tithing and are not combined with animals from before or after.

steps.title: Animals born within one tithing year join together
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, all animals born from 1 תשרי through 29 אלול count as one year's group for מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: All animals born from 1 תשרי until 29 אלול can be combined together for tithing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws the practical result of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון's view. Their year runs from 1 תשרי to 29 אלול, so every animal born inside that span is part of the same tithing group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה works by counting animals in groups of ten, and only animals from the same year can be counted together. Since this view starts the year on 1 תשרי, the whole span up to 29 אלול is one unit. The last day, 29 אלול, is the deadline we saw in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: they join together (they can be counted in the same group of ten)
the tithe of animals: every tenth newborn animal is set aside as holy

phrases.english: All those born from the first of Tishrei
phrases.notes: Per רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון

phrases.english: until the twenty-ninth of Elul
these join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the year-boundary of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון to the question of which animals combine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals born between 1 תשרי and 29 אלול combine for מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: The new year splits groups, but a gathering date does not
steps.stepSummary: Five animals born before ראש השנה and five born after it do not combine. Five born before a גורן and five born after it do combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five born before ראש השנה and five after ראש השנה do not join. Five born before the gathering time and five after the gathering time do join.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts two kinds of dates. ראש השנה is a true wall between years. A גורן (gathering time) is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the new year changes which 'year' an animal belongs to, so animals on either side of ראש השנה cannot be tithed together. A גורן is just a checkpoint within the same year, so animals on either side of it still count as one group.

keyTerms.meaning: a set gathering time for tithing animals (literally 'threshing floor')
the new year, which divides one tithing year from the next

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גורן is a new 'year'. It is only a deadline inside the year. Only ראש השנה separates the groups.

phrases.english: Five before Rosh HaShana
and five after Rosh HaShana
do not join together.
Five before the gathering time
and five after the gathering time
these do join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה לְאַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of step 18 with two contrasting cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראש השנה separates tithing groups; a גורן does not.

steps.title: So what are the three gathering times for?
steps.stepSummary: If a גורן does not split the groups, why did the חכמים set three גרנות for מעשר בהמה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why were three gathering times stated for animal tithe?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks an obvious follow-up. It has just shown that a גורן does not separate groups, so what is its purpose? This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 removed the most natural reason for the גרנות, namely dividing the animals into groups. The משנה must now give the גורן a different job.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (if what was just said is true)

phrases.english: If so,
why were three gathering times stated
for animal tithe?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ שָׁלֹשׁ גֳּרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the גרנות after step 19 showed they do not divide groups.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What legal function do the three גרנות have?

steps.title: The gathering time marks when slaughter becomes forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Before the גורן you may sell or slaughter the animals. Once it arrives you may not slaughter before tithing, but if you did, you are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before the gathering time arrives, it is permitted to sell and slaughter. Once the gathering time arrives, one may not slaughter, but if he slaughtered, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question. The גורן is the point after which you should not slaughter animals that have not yet been tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the גורן, the owner may freely sell or slaughter his animals. After it, he should tithe first. Even so, if he went ahead and slaughtered, he is פטור: the slaughtered animal is exempt from מעשר בהמה, because only live animals are counted for the tithe. So the גורן creates a prohibition on slaughtering, but it does not create a tithe obligation that stays with an animal that was already slaughtered.
steps.whatToRemember: ראש השנה divides the groups of animals. The גורן is a deadline: after it you should not slaughter untithed animals. If you did, you are still פטור.

phrases.english: For until the gathering time has arrived
it is permitted to sell and to slaughter;
once the gathering time arrives, he may not slaughter,
but if he slaughtered, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by defining the גורן's function.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גורן sets the point after which slaughtering untithed animals is forbidden, though a person who slaughtered anyway is exempt.

steps.title: Why specifically three gathering times?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why there are exactly three גרנות a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is special about three?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the חכמים set three גרנות, not more and not fewer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explained what a גורן does, but not why there are three of them. The גמרא wants a reason for the number.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is special about three?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא, asking about the number of גרנות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason there are exactly three גרנות.

steps.title: Three gathering times match three birthing seasons
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא explains that the three dates correspond to three groups of births: early-season, late-season, and summer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: Corresponding to the early-born ones, the late-born ones, and the summer-born ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא answers that animals give birth in three main waves, so there is one gathering time for each wave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals tend to give birth in three seasons. A גורן after each wave means the newborns are gathered and tithed soon after a large group is born.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who explains the number three

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said:
Corresponding to the early ones, the late ones, and the summer ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three גרנות match the three birthing seasons: early, late, and summer.

steps.title: Why these particular dates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the גרנות fall on these specific times. It introduces רבי תנחום, whose answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about these times? רבי תנחום, son of רב חייא, of כפר עכו, said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second question: granted there are three, why are they set at these specific times, before פסח, שבועות, and סוכות? It then names רבי תנחום, whose answer appears on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר שילא explained the number three, but not the timing. The גמרא now wants to know why each גורן is placed right before a festival. The answer begins at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sage who answers why these times were chosen

phrases.english: And what is special about these times?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum, son of Rav Ḥiyya, said
phrases.notes: This attribution introduces the answer, which continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: of the village of Akko:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 23 by asking about the timing rather than the number.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the three גרנות are set at these specific times (before the festivals).
